children: A real-world study of 294,499 U.S. veterans aged 65 and older found mNEXSPIKE was associated with 35.9% lower risk of medically attended COVID-19 and 47.0% lower risk of COVID-19-associated hospitalization versus Comirnaty. The observational findings do not establish causality.
The comparative result may support mNEXSPIKE's positioning among older adults, but the study is observational and does not establish causality.
The primary outcome favored mNEXSPIKE; no prior-period comparison was provided.
The large cohort adds real-world evidence, though the predominantly older, male veteran population may limit generalizability.
This exploratory result may broaden the clinical evidence, but it is associative and should not be read as proof of causation.

This adds real-world comparative evidence for an existing Moderna vaccine rather than reporting a new product launch or financial result. Further evidence in broader populations, alongside commercial uptake or revenue disclosures, would be needed to establish a larger business catalyst.
from Moderna, Inc. distributed by ACCESS Newswire.
